items.title: 67848_Jimmy McPartland oral history interview
items.q: I went down to New Orleans with Glen Miller and Smith Bullew and Ray McKinley was on drums then. And worked down there for six months.

ctx.x: To take care of the baby and I went on the road with the show. And when I came back why she had gotten together with her sister and they were both, I mean Hannah was going to get a divorce from Roger Wolf Kahn and my wife decided to divorce me and marry somebody with a lot of money. And that broke me up. That's the thing that, that's the thing that broke me up.

So I just, as a matter of fact, I went down to New Orleans with Glen Miller and Smith Bullew and Ray McKinley was on drums then. And worked down there for six months. But when I came back, seeing the whole situation. Dorothy had gotten married again, my wife and had gotten the baby, she had the baby and everything so I just sort of lost heart, you know. And not knowing how to cope with the situation, I just couldn't even play.

So I decided to go back to Chicago which I did and join my brother with a little outfit called the 'Embassy Four'Quartet' and we played that in the Dalmer House for a little while. And then I didn't care for that, it was too commercial, the music was. And I decided to get my own band. That's when I went into the 'Three Deuces' there.
